review[].name: ["Your perfect template for a platformer - or for the 2D game of your dreams! Beginner friendly!", "Mainly for Beginners", "Solid, Fluid, Easy, Outstanding and Polished."]
review[].reviewbody: ["The author has created a platformer engine. An engine that if you run one of his demo levels, you can simply rebuild on it to create your own. Or you can study those demo levels to understand how everything works in Unity. Or read his scripts if you're so inclined and understand how a simple script can move a character around, or make it perform an action. Personally, just by reading his code and adding more, I will be creating a proper platformer RPG, because the engine allows for extensive building on top of it. This requires reading on my part, but the author's coding structure and variable names are so clear and consistent, that it has made this difficult endeavour a very fun and creative process for me. There are also a few youtube videos that explain how to extend the pre-existing classes to add your own code and expand the project. Most importantly, the engine is built with Raycasts, which means that it is not physics based. The lack of physics make the controls feel like the old school platformers where a single push of the arrow will take you only a little bit further forward and not", "This is not a tool meant for intermediate or advanced developers. tl;dr: Beginners can learn a lot, but advanced developers who need more customization will be better off building their own engine. The Pros: - Lots of configurable character controller traits - Easy to jump right in and start making a game with many common features found in games - Fantastic for beginners who are learning a wide breadth of skills. This package allows beginners to easily test level design techniques, as well as explore the code-base to get an idea how common features are implemented. - Great for GameJams and Prototyping. - Developer is very responsive and cares about his customer's satisfaction. - The engine is still being improved on a regular basis and the developer is open to suggestions and bug fixes The Cons: - The character controller is very buggy. When you jump up and hit your head on the roof, there is a chance you'll fall very fast. Jumping upwards into a slope has unpredictable behavior - sometimes you fall, sometimes you stick to the slope, sometimes you're pushed away from the slope. Running and hitting your head on the roof saps all of your horizontal", "This asset is truly outstanding. The mechanics are "deployment ready" meaning I would feel comfortable putting my own art into the current structure and releasing a title. The code is well commented and easy to understand/implement and the character animation state machine is very well put together. No complaints here and it'll be even better of a package with documentation. It's easy enough to dive into without documentation because of the commenting in the code but some tutorials could go a long way with folks who might feel otherwise. Thanks for the wonderful asset! I'll be using it in an upcoming title. EDIT: My mistake for not noticing the documentation! It is indeed there and very clear/easy to understand. After working with this engine for a few months intensely (it sat there for a while while I worked on some other projects) I'm so pleased with how polished, stable and efficient this engine is. I've been able to use it to create a great base and create all the functionality I've needed for my game mechanics by extending classes and adding onto the engine without any major conflicts so far. I recommend this highly to anyone who's planning on creating"]

review[].reviewbody: ["In my opinion this is one of the best/most complete unity character controller based fps controllers, it has the important stuff that most of the other more expensive kits lack like moving platform support especially if your game has any forward/backward or rotating platform objects your character is going to land on, then this is important for it to work correctly, and with it being based on unity character controller makes it easy to use for multiplayer networking like with Photon too, jump is cool with bunny hoop support (quick succession jumps) and air control is a great idea but this needs a bit more refinement as side strafing in the air and landing repeatedly seems to cause a weird amount of speed to be generated in the strafe direction even with the acceleration turned down but air control is good too just needs a little more work in my opinion, ladder support works great and head bob management is very good too but the best thing is the price it is extremely well priced for all you get, and that’s without mentioning the cool footstep system too. It could do with double jump(jump again while in air option),prone, climbing,", "I really like this thing. It provides a lot of what I've been looking for, especially look smoothing when strafing as the standard FPS controller jitters horribly. I had to adjust the DoMouse function to look at individual mouse sensitivity values instead of it's current sensitivity that applies to both x and y so that I could allow for inverted look. Very easy fix though. Second, I would really like a way to initialize mouse look. Basically re-set it. I have moments where animation takes over my camera movement and I would like the mouse look values to equal the end values of the camera's current rotation after so I can have seamless transitions back into game. I'll figure it out though but it would be great if it was built in. - Allow for invert X and Y options so you don't have to code it yourself. - Allow for re-initialization of the mouse look function so you can have more control over camera movement with animated sequences. Overall, awesome stuff!", "I liked the asset, though there are some comments. 1. When pushing objects, they can often be pushed through a wall 2. I would like to be able to turn off horizontal movement while climbing stairs. 3. when climbing stairs, the character incorrectly calculates the location of the head and the camera flies through the roof"]

review[].name: ["Great value for abundant material", "Beautiful Assets, Great Value, A Few Minor Issues", "Excellent Deal"]
review[].reviewbody: ["This product comes packed with hundreds of objects and a few scenes. The quality of the objects is a little inconsistent, but enough of it is good to make this a steal. I mean, some people will charge you $5 for a standalone grandfather clock, so $5 for all these interiors is amazing. Some people have complained about lack of LOD. I can sort of understand, but it would be a lot of work to add LOD to everything. In any case, it might not well suited to mobile games, but it should be fine for PC or console.", "I'm very impressed with the quality of the models contained here, especially at the price. They look just as nice as they do in the trailer. To complement these excellent meshes and textures is a great LOD system to help keep things efficient. The package does not immediately work with HDRP but can be automatically converted without issue. That being said, I do have a few irritations. I wish that the prefabs were more modular, for one. For instance, the clock prefab looks great, you can't access the individual components such as the clock's hands or pendulum, which is a shame because that means it has to be a static piece that looks out of place with the rest of the beautiful assets. Another issue is that the doors don't seem to be made for the doorframes and always leave some open space. I thought I was just setting up the frames or doors incorrectly, but I've seen others comment on this issue. Also, something that you should be aware of that I didn't pick up on is that the furniture contains imperfections such as scratches and scuffs. This can lead to a more realistic and "lived-in" feel, especially for", "I'm not sure why all the complaints about High Poly Meshes, after popping a few of these into blender, most of the polycounts seem very fair. Good Edge loops and consistent mesh flow. Nothing seems excessively busy and for non animated meshes you can always dissolve them down further for your LOD's, although having the LOD's included would be nice, for 5 dollars you are getting a wide array of well made meshes / textures. I really can't complain, especially at such an amazing price. It's a steal. EDIT: I forgot to mention, the entire package is highly modular in it's piece design. Found a few small issues.. one of the bed posts has z-fighting as the faces were duplicated resulting in a flickering post.. easy to resolve as a work around for others: just pop the object into blender and delete the second layer of faces around that post, the uvmapping is identical so should be fine to just update the prefab.. Would be nice to have that fixed in future verisons. :)"]

review[].name: ["Amazing Support", "Decent for Pokemon Go, but not much else", "Go Map is an amazingly great asset"]
review[].reviewbody: ["The developer(Alan) is really helpful. I have been looking into integrating GO Map with other 3rd party plugins and systems that weren't originally supported. At the same time I was trying to get everything working together, Alan was doing the same from his end. I also talked with him about the aim of my project and he was passionate and enthusiastic to help me solve it. Especially anything to do with iOS and AR. This system is also user friendly which helps a lot.", "There are some pros and cons: Pros: -Decent documentation -Good examples (can copy/paste in most cases) -Easy enough API (for basic implementation) Cons: -LONG wait on any support requests (days to weeks), and even then developer may just say, "I don't know how to help you" and ghost you... -Plugin can only fake directional light. If you are trying to use spotlights, point lights, or anything inside the environment on a scene with 3D terrain (for instance street lights, headlights on cars, etc), it breaks, and cannot accept light in some directions -If you don't know the order in which things are drawn, you spend hours tracking down why the API is not working. And then the developer may send you down a road that is not relevant to your problem. Here's your answer: if something is not working properly, look for the class which can trigger other functions after everything else is drawn, and coordinates are set. That's most likely your issue. Unless it's lighting. On that, you're out of luck. Overall, my company wasted 5-weeks going back and forth with the Developer regarding the lighting issue and a few other issues (which we had to solve ourselves) before", "I highly recommend it. A very well put together pack and if you should require help to answer how to use it, then support from the developer is excellent and very fast. Alan the developer was helping me with tips on building a railway viaduct only this week by direct emails, brilliant stuff Alan thank you, your tips on feature coding, worked like a dream. Thank's Alan. I am a semi-retired CAD railway draughtsman living in London, England. Not being a C# coder, I know only the basics of a classes and scripting. Wanting to create Android mapping applications, Go Map was the obvious choice. I purchased Go Map back in 2017, since then I have been exploring the potential of real time mapping using Go Map. The Go Map pack contains a wealth of demo scenes to utilise the potential of vector mapping available from the likes of Mapbox. The included scripts expose a wealth of variables to the user, in a friendly user interface, ideal for non coders like me, so very quickly I had usable mapping results that looked good and apps that also worked well on my Samsung mobile, with no glitches or worries about coding."]

(Proving it's hard to use) If we only use it as components then yes it helps with the UI a little bit but it really only worth at most 15 dollars.", "It seems like you can do a lot with this asset. But I feel it needs a lot more online tutorials, just a few examples of what you can use it for in game - maybe a forum where people can support each other on how to use it. review[].reviewbody: ["It's products like these which are extremely necessary for indie developers, allowing them to create works of art in minutes, things like these allow people to really realize their dreams without the added hassle and demotivation . Just look at the transformation between the Japanese monument - it has a basic color scheme and then it transforms completely with Ambient Occlusion and the worn look - wow!", "The Good: The final results are great! I can see the potential of this tool. Well designed toolsets for artists - without the need for programming! Right up my street. Great for 512 res textures. Probably really good for mobile developers. However, if you are doing high end stuff.. The Bad: When I saw the video, showcasing this asset, I was blown away. It was just what I needed. So I purchased it, and started copying the steps in the video.. I was shocked at how long it took to generate the noise, curvature data etc.. I am running an i7 with 32gb ram and SSHD, GTX 970 ~ all overclocked. In the video, the generation times are edited out. When I was trying to create a 2048 texture, I went and made a cup of tea, then did the cleaning, and it was ready. I normally work really fast, so this doesn't fit into my workflow. It needs multithreading or something.. I don't know, I am not a programmer. I would come back to use this if it were even 2X faster. More speed please!", "It is possible that this is the best thing I have ever bought on the asset store. One of my problems in designing survival horror environments is that I have ten million assets and most of them look too good to be real. The texturing is just too perfect in most cases and doesn't look worn enough to be scary or atmospheric. You run them through this tool with a little tweaking and you can turn a spanking new object into a dingy old antique that looks ready to fall apart. I had a really good looking low poly vintage phone with one 256x256 texture on it and it was all pastels and looked like plastic at runtime. One pass with this tool and it now looks 80 years old and encrusted with rust. Truly indispensable if you are a designer who does it all on his own and you have no artist on your team to help with these kinds of problems."]

review[].reviewbody: ["This system is put together really well. I think I've been waiting for the new version for about a year, but it was worth the wait. Perhaps the system is designed mostly with RPGs in mind, but honestly so many types of games have a need for a way to manage stats. It doesn't need to be a big epic RPG either. Action RPG or RPG-Lite games can benefit too, for example I am working on a Vampire Survivors-Like game and the new level reward system is perfect for that. Great job!", "GDTK save my time a lot", "With the goal of assembling a versatile RPG framework, I recently combined GDTK:Stats, GDTK:Inventory (beta), and a few other third-party assets into a project. Though I am still trying to make improvements, I’ve learned much about GDTK:Stats and how it can work with various sub-systems. Here are some of my experiences in four areas: Features, Workflow, Integrations and Maintainability. FEATURES: GDTK:Stats is good enough for Fifth Edition D&D, though one could forgo some advanced features for non-RPG use if needed. The component attached to the player character (or NPC) covers most stat creations. You can use formulas to create second-order stats whose values depend on other stats and variables. The advanced RPG-related features are available via the Stats Database window. There you can design character classes, backgrounds, and races, set up level rewards, define status conditions (e.g., hunger) and effects (e.g., freeze), and do many more. What sets it apart from others I’ve seen is the level and flexibility of customizations allowed, often via the use of included perk, trait, add-on, and unlocking features. For example, I can set conditional rules for a reward system that gives out different rewards (or reward categories) dependent on the player character's race, class,"]
